issue: Numeric part 'rates' scores a correct one-decimal answer as wrong. The exhibit states every rate to one decimal (4.9%, 10.3%, 9.2%) and the prompt gives no rounding instruction, but sdr is keyed 3.33 with tolerance 0.01 and asr 6.97 with tolerance 0.02. A candidate who answers 3.3 and 7.0 (consistent with the exhibit's precision) loses both cells, a third of the simulation's 6 cells.
evidence: Scoring is absolute (src/lib/tbsScoring.ts withinTolerance: |given - expected| <= tolerance). sdr: 2/60 = 3.3333%; |3.3 - 3.33| = 0.03 > 0.01 -> marked wrong. asr: 10.3 - 3.3 = 7.0; |7.0 - 6.97| = 0.03 > 0.02 -> marked wrong. 10.3 - 3.333 = 6.967 and 10.3 - 3.33 = 6.97 are accepted, so the only thing separating right from wrong is an unstated rounding convention. My blind answers 3.33/6.97 matched the key, but 3.3/7.0 is equally correct.
source: AICPA Audit Guide, Audit Sampling (evaluation of attribute samples: allowance for sampling risk = upper deviation rate - sample deviation rate); src/lib/tbsScoring.ts
fix: Either add 'Round percentages to two decimal places (e.g., 12.34)' to the part prompt, or widen tolerances so both roundings score: sdr tolerance 0.04 (accepts 3.30-3.37), asr tolerance 0.04 (accepts 6.93-7.01). Mention both roundings in the explanations.

issue: The lesson cites PCAOB AS 2201 and AS 2301 but presents the AU-C 330 rotation rule (prior-year evidence; test at least once every third audit) without saying it is an AICPA/nonissuer rule. In a PCAOB integrated audit each year must stand on its own: controls relied on are tested every year (prior-year knowledge only reduces extent; benchmarking is limited to automated controls). aud-toc-03, aud-toc-26 and flashcard aud-toc-f3 state no framework, so under an integrated audit their 'every year' / 'No' distractors would be the correct answers.
evidence: Lesson keyTakeaways: 'Prior-year evidence may be used for unchanged controls ... each control must be tested at least once every third audit'; citations list 'PCAOB AS 2301 and AS 2201' with no contrast anywhere in the body. aud-toc-03 choice (a) 'Every year, in every audit' is explained as wrong because 'Rotation is permitted' - not true under AS 2201. A 2005 SEC-hosted statement on AS 2 (now AS 2201) records that rotation of testing was suggested and 'the PCAOB rejected this suggestion requiring that each year must stand on its own' (https://sec.gov/news/press/4-497/lee033105.pdf). AS 2201.57-.61 (subsequent-year knowledge reduces testing) and AS 2201.B28-.B33 (benchmarking of automated controls) - paragraph numbers from memory.
fix: Add a one-line contrast to the 'Using prior-year evidence' section and the takeaway: 'Rotation is an AICPA (nonissuer) rule; in a PCAOB integrated audit, relied-on controls are tested every year (benchmarking applies only to automated controls).' Add 'In an audit of a nonissuer under GAAS' to the stems of aud-toc-03 and aud-toc-26 and to the front of aud-toc-f3; optionally add one item contrasting the two frameworks.

issue: Skill (and difficulty) badly inflated on pure-recall items: aud-toc-14, -26 are labeled evaluation/3, aud-toc-24, -25 analysis/3, aud-toc-27 evaluation/3. Each asks the learner to recall a single rule, with obviously wrong distractors. Twin items testing the same facts carry much lower labels (aud-toc-chk2 application/2 for the significant-risk rule; aud-toc-02 application/2 for interim roll-forward; aud-toc-03 remembering/1 for rotation).
evidence: Blueprint verbs: Evaluation = evaluate/judge; Analysis = analyze, reconcile, investigate discrepancies; R&U = recall/identify. aud-toc-14 = recall AU-C 330.15 (remembering). aud-toc-26 'Yes, with limits' = recall AU-C 330.14 (remembering). aud-toc-25 'Rollforward evidence' = recall AU-C 330.12 (remembering). aud-toc-24 'Test the one instance' = remembering/application. aud-toc-27 'systemic deviation -> not effective' = application. Practice-pool mix now R 18.5% / A 44.4% / An 22.2% / E 14.8% vs Blueprint R 30-40 / A 30-40 / An 15-25 / E 5-15; the inflation pushes R below range and E to the cap. Difficulty 3 on these items also inverts the easy-to-hard order (items 14-27 are the easiest yet labeled hardest).
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Exam Blueprints, AUD skill definitions (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md); AU-C 330.12, .14, .15
fix: Relabel: aud-toc-14 remembering/1; aud-toc-24 remembering/1; aud-toc-25 remembering/1; aud-toc-26 remembering/2; aud-toc-27 application/1. If the module needs evaluation items, write genuine ones (e.g., given deviation facts, decide reliance and the substantive response).

issue: Skill labels one level off: aud-toc-09 evaluation (it asks for the first procedural step; analysis at most); aud-toc-17, -18, -20 analysis (single-concept identification; application); aud-toc-13 application (verbatim recall that inquiry alone is insufficient, the same fact aud-toc-22 labels remembering).
evidence: aud-toc-13 and aud-toc-22 test the identical rule (AU-C 330.10(a)) yet carry application/1 and remembering/2. aud-toc-09 key 'Investigate the causes and reassess planned reliance' restates AU-C 330.17 - no judgment among competing evaluations is required. aud-toc-17/18/20 each have one plausible option and need no analysis of data.
fix: aud-toc-09 -> analysis (or application); aud-toc-17, -18, -20 -> application; aud-toc-13 -> remembering.

issue: Trap labels don't describe the misconception: 'partial-computation' is used on non-numeric distractors with no computation (aud-toc-chk1 d, aud-toc-16 d, aud-toc-17 a/b/c, aud-toc-18 c/d, aud-toc-25 c, aud-x2-34 a), and 'wrong-sign' on distractors with no sign (aud-toc-26 d 'Only for fraud risks', aud-toc-27 d 'Increase reliance').
evidence: No item in this module has calc=true (cues.md: calc {False: 30}). aud-toc-chk1 d 'Only in integrated audits of issuers' is a scope error (overgeneralization/wrong-rule); aud-toc-17 a 'Whether a sign-off exists' is a partial-understanding error, not a computation; aud-x2-34 a 'a walkthrough provides sufficient evidence' is wrong-classification (design vs operation); aud-toc-27 d is 'reversed'; aud-toc-26 d is 'wrong-rule'.
fix: Relabel: chk1 d -> overgeneralization; toc-16 d -> wrong-rule; toc-17 a -> wrong-rule, b/c -> irrelevant-fact; toc-18 c/d -> irrelevant-fact; toc-25 c -> wrong-rule; toc-26 d -> wrong-rule; toc-27 d -> reversed; x2-34 a -> wrong-classification.

issue: Answer cue: absolutes appear only in the distractors, and the key is the single hedged option, so a test-wise learner can pick it without knowing the rule.
evidence: aud-toc-10: b, c and d all contain 'always'; key a says 'may not'. aud-toc-chk1: a 'Whenever', b 'Whenever', d 'Only'; key c has no qualifier. aud-toc-26: a 'No, never', c 'Yes, indefinitely', d 'Only for fraud risks' vs key 'Yes, with limits' (the hedged middle). aud-toc-14: c 'Only if it changes', d 'Never again'. aud-toc-25: c 'only', d 'all items'. (cues.md flagged each.)
fix: Rewrite distractors as plausible, unqualified misconceptions, e.g., aud-toc-10: 'Because automated processing makes inherent risk high', 'Because the PCAOB requires an ICFR opinion', 'Because revenue is a presumed fraud risk'; aud-toc-26: 'Yes, if management represents that the control hasn't changed', 'Yes, for up to five years'.

issue: Implausible distractors leave one live option, so these items don't discriminate. aud-toc-17 also has a vague stem ('What is key?').
evidence: aud-toc-17: 'Only the reviewer's job title', 'Only the report's format'. aud-toc-18: 'Only the report's layout', 'Only the user's training record'. aud-toc-20: 'It doesn't need evaluating'. aud-toc-21: 'Management's integrity', 'Industry conditions'. aud-toc-24: 'It can't be tested', 'Test it monthly' (for an annual control). aud-toc-27: 'Ignore it as one deviation', 'Keep full reliance on it', 'Increase reliance'.
fix: Use misconceptions candidates actually hold, e.g., aud-toc-17: 'Whether the reviewer signed every month', 'Whether the reviewer is independent of preparation', 'Whether the report agrees to the GL' vs key 'Whether the review is precise enough to detect a material misstatement and outliers are investigated'; aud-toc-24: 'Expand to a sample of 25 by testing prior years', 'Substitute a walkthrough'; aud-toc-27: 'Extend the sample and rely if no further deviations are found'.

issue: Stem omits the condition that triggers the rule ('the auditor plans to rely on it'), and choice (a)'s explanation overstates it: 'Controls over significant risks are tested every year.' AU-C 330.15 requires current-period testing only if the auditor relies on those controls; the auditor may instead respond to a significant risk with substantive procedures alone (including tests of details).
evidence: Stem: 'A control that mitigates a significant risk was tested last year and hasn't changed. How often must it be tested?' Compare aud-toc-chk2 and aud-toc-f4, which correctly say 'if the auditor plans to rely on it' / 'If relied on'. The same overstatement appears in content/aud/review/aud-high-yield.md line 27 ('significant-risk controls must be tested every year') - outside this batch.
source: AU-C 330.15; AU-C 330.22 (substantive-only response to a significant risk includes tests of details)
fix: Stem: '...hasn't changed, and the auditor plans to rely on it this year. When must it be tested?' Choice (a) explanation: 'If relied on, controls over significant risks must be tested in the current period; rotation isn't allowed.'

issue: Distractor explanations are false as written: (c) 'Management's integrity' and (d) 'Industry conditions' are both explained as 'Not directly by the auditor.' The auditor does evaluate both - industry, regulatory and other external factors in the risk assessment, and management's integrity in acceptance and the control environment. The point is only that tests of controls don't evaluate them.
evidence: AU-C 315 requires an understanding of relevant industry, regulatory and other external factors; client acceptance (AU-C 210 / SQMS 1) and the control-environment assessment consider management's integrity.
source: AU-C 315 (understanding the entity and its environment); AU-C 210; SQMS No. 1
fix: (c): 'Integrity is considered in acceptance and the control-environment assessment, not by tests of controls.' (d): 'Industry conditions are part of understanding the entity (risk assessment), not tests of controls.'

issue: Thin, fragmentary or circular explanations that don't teach the rule: aud-toc-18 key 'Correct. Information used in the control.'; aud-toc-19 key 'Correct. It operates consistently.' (no mention that this depends on effective change-management ITGCs and an unchanged program); aud-toc-24 key 'Correct. A single occurrence is tested.' (circular); aud-toc-10 (c) 'This applies to nonissuers too, based on the situation.' (doesn't say why the PCAOB claim is wrong).
evidence: Explanations quoted from items.json. Rules they should state: AU-C 500.09 / AS 1105.10 (test accuracy and completeness of information produced by the entity used in a control); automated controls function consistently unless the program changes, so one instance suffices only with effective program-change and access ITGCs (AU-C 330 application guidance; AS 2201.B28-.B33); AU-C 330.08(b) applies under GAAS and PCAOB alike, and PCAOB standards don't require control testing in every FS audit.
fix: Rewrite each correct-choice explanation to state the rule and its condition (e.g., aud-toc-18: 'A control is only as good as the data it uses: the auditor tests the report's completeness and accuracy, or the ITGCs and application controls over it.'). aud-toc-10 (c): 'Wrong: the requirement comes from the situation (AU-C 330.08(b)), which applies to nonissuers too; PCAOB standards don't require control testing in every audit of financial statements.'

issue: Lesson-item alignment: the lesson (322 body words) has no section on the extent of tests of controls or on evaluating results, yet 11 items plus the exam TBS test exactly that. Untaught: sample-size drivers (tolerable rate, risk of overreliance, control frequency); management review controls and precision; reliability of information produced by the entity used in a control; 'no misstatements found doesn't prove a control effective' (AU-C 330.16); infrequent/annual controls; evaluating deviations (cause, deliberate deviation and fraud, systemic vs isolated, upper deviation rate vs tolerable rate). The sampling terms are taught only in aud-sampling, which comes later (aud-u6, Area III), so aud-toc-15, aud-x2-44 and the TBS rely on a later module.
evidence: The lesson covers only when to test, procedure types, design vs operation, and prior-year/interim evidence; its only line on deviations is the takeaway 'A deviation doesn't automatically mean the control failed; the auditor evaluates its cause...'. grep of the lessons for aud-it-controls, aud-internal-control, aud-risk-response and aud-evidence-assertions finds no teaching of management-review-control precision or IPE testing. aud-sampling lesson lines 34-35 teach the sample-size factors and upper deviation rate vs tolerable rate, but it is sequenced after this module.
source: AU-C 330.09-.11, .16-.17; AU-C 500.09; AU-C 530.12-.13; content/sections/aud.yaml module order
fix: Add a short section 'Extent of testing and evaluating deviations': more reliance means more evidence; frequency-based sample sizes (annual 1, quarterly 2, monthly 2-5, weekly 5-15, daily 20-40, many times a day 25-60); one instance of an automated control with effective ITGCs; MRC precision and IPE; AU-C 330.16; and a deviation decision tree (investigate cause -> deliberate? consider fraud -> systemic? not effective -> compare upper deviation rate with tolerable rate, with a forward reference to aud-sampling). This also makes 'minutes: 14' realistic (the current page reads in about 8-10 minutes).

issue: Within-module redundancy: the same fact is tested the same way several times. 'Inquiry alone is insufficient' appears in aud-toc-pre1, aud-toc-13, aud-toc-22 and flashcard f2, and again as distractors in aud-toc-06, aud-x2-22 and aud-x2-34. aud-toc-25 repeats aud-toc-02 (interim roll-forward; also f6). aud-toc-14 repeats aud-toc-chk2 almost word for word (also f4). Mock item aud-x2-22 reuses practice item aud-toc-06's key wording ('Inspecting a year-wide sample...'), so practiced learners recognize the key on the mock.
evidence: aud-toc-chk2: 'A control over a significant risk was tested last year and hasn't changed...'; aud-toc-14: 'A control that mitigates a significant risk was tested last year and hasn't changed...'. aud-toc-06 key 'Inspecting a year-wide sample for evidence of performance'; aud-x2-22 key 'Inspecting a year-wide sample of large cleared checks' against the same distractor pattern (inquiry, policy manual, substantive procedure).
fix: Replace aud-toc-22 and aud-toc-25 with items on untaught angles (e.g., indirect controls, or the extent of roll-forward evidence when interim results were poor). Turn aud-toc-14 into a scenario with a significant risk where the auditor chooses between relying on controls and a substantive-only response. Reword aud-x2-22's key and distractors (e.g., 'Select checks over $10,000 written throughout the year and inspect each for two authorized signatures' against 'Reperform the bank reconciliation for December').

issue: Cross-module redundancy with aud-sampling and aud-internal-control. aud-toc-15 (lower tolerable deviation rate -> larger sample) duplicates aud-sa-16, aud-sa-22 and aud-x3-05, so the same fact is tested the same way 4 times. aud-x2-44 (upper limit above the tolerable rate -> reduce reliance, expand substantive) duplicates aud-ic-26, aud-sa-02, aud-sa-24 and aud-x3-44, plus TBS row ev.b.
evidence: aud-sa-16 'raises the tolerable deviation rate ... sample size? It decreases'; aud-sa-22 'If the tolerable deviation rate increases...? It decreases'; aud-x3-05 'decreases the tolerable deviation rate...? It increases'; aud-ic-26 'deviation rate above the tolerable rate... Assess control risk higher'.
fix: Re-point aud-toc-15 at a sample-size driver not covered elsewhere (expected deviation rate, or frequency for a weekly control). Make aud-x2-44 a two-step application (e.g., give the sample size, deviations and upper deviation rate and ask for the effect on the substantive response for a specific assertion), or drop it from the mock in favour of an untested task.

issue: Flashcard is incomplete in a way that can mislead. The front 'Rotation rule for unchanged controls' and the back 'Test each control at least once every third audit...' omit that rotation (1) excludes controls over significant risks, which must be tested in the current period if relied on, and (2) requires evidence each year that the control hasn't changed (inquiry plus observation or inspection). A significant-risk control is also an 'unchanged control'.
evidence: AU-C 330.13 (establish continuing relevance with inquiry combined with observation or inspection); AU-C 330.14(b) (every third audit; some controls each audit); AU-C 330.15 (significant risks: current period). The lesson's worked example states both conditions; the card does not.
fix: Back: 'Unchanged controls NOT over a significant risk: confirm no change each year (inquiry + observation/inspection), test at least once every third audit, and test some controls every audit (AICPA/nonissuer rule).'

issue: The simulation is thin for an exam-pool TBS budgeted at 20 minutes: 6 cells, two of them binary 'Rely / Do not rely' dropdowns (50% by guessing), and the 'overall conclusion' key for control C is a process ('Weigh its nature...') rather than a conclusion, against two straw-man options.
evidence: Parts: rates (2 numeric), ev (4 dropdown; a and b have 2 options each, cq has 3 options of which 'Ignore it, because only a single deviation...' is implausible). Most AUD TBS take about 15-18 minutes for 8-15 cells; this one needs about 8-10.
source: AICPA exam format (AUD: 7 TBS); review brief §2 per-TBS checks
fix: Add a part asking for the substantive response per control (nature/timing/extent options) and a deficiency classification for control C (deficiency / significant deficiency / material weakness / evaluate further). Reword the cq options to conclusions: 'Do not rely as planned; evaluate as possible management override and fraud risk' vs 'Rely as planned; the rate is within tolerable' vs 'Extend the sample; rely if no further deviations'. Or reduce minutes to 10-12.

The reconstructed Blueprint places 'Perform tests of the operating effectiveness of controls' in Area III (Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence, Group D topic 'Tests of controls'). Only the decision to test controls (planned response) is Area II. If so, mock area weights overstate Area II.
evidence: review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv row AUD-III.D.1.1 'Perform tests of the operating effectiveness of controls' (status uncertain); the blueprint-notes.md Area III scope text quotes '...performing procedures to obtain evidence including tests of controls'.
fix: Confirm against the official Blueprint PDF. If confirmed, tag the operating-effectiveness and evaluation items (and the TBS) as Area III for mock balancing, keeping the 'when to test' objective in Area II.
